He left Sichitinga â Sichitinga. Her older brother went off with his wife, he's [StN]: leave or remain?gone. Sichitinga stayed behind and thought: "Where shall I go? I'll go somewhere!" Sichitinga went, started singing and left. A raven flew by. "Kuk, Sichitinga, I take you [as my wife]!" "Early in the morning, when the weather is fine,Â¹â¾ you scream a lot! I'm scared of you!" Sichitinga went on. The mouse under the log says: " Chi-chi chi-chi, I take you, Sichitinga, [to be my wife]!" She married a mouse. She went into the mouse's yurt. She came and went into the yurt. The old mother mouse and the old father mouse live together with the mouse. Sichitinga came to the mouse. She feeds Sichitinga. She steals: she steals all kinds of things, meat, bread â she eats. The mouse was killed for it. Her father went off to look for the mouse. She stole from the storage. She was killed for stealing from the storage. Her father came home and says, "Because of[StN]: RUS: preposition and it's valency Sichitinga!" Her father says, "A child was killed because of you!" He says to Sichitinga: "Today the patternfirewood will be finely cut! The raven will come and hit you with a big firewood![StN]: INSTR -Äi It's finely cut!" Sichitinga cuts the chips finely, they have been crushed like kindling shavings. In the evening a raven flew in, entered the yurt and said: "Oh, Sichitinga! I told you to marry me! You didn't marry me?! You married the mouse!" He took the [StN]: DECAUS + chopped wood, hit it and the kindling shavings broke.
